issues.detail: Runnable code is almost entirely Node/Express with SimpleWebAuthn; Python and Java get only a brief non-runnable sketch (Python registration only, Java a single dependency line).
The two Examples are short prose scenarios without concrete runnable inputs and outputs, so they are simplistic compared with the code in the Instructions.

scenarios.name: passkey-registration-endpoints
scenarios.rationale: B stores the challenge server-side with a 300-second TTL and an atomic read-and-delete, and it meets the rest of the rubric. A keeps the challenge in the session with no explicit TTL, which is weaker on the TTL requirement, and it passes `req.body.response.transports` instead of the verified `credential.transports`.

scenarios.name: login-verification-counter-and-session
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely — allowCredentials as { id, transports }, a challenge bound to the session, a credential object, newCounter stored, an HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookie and startAuthentication({ optionsJSON }) — while B leaves out allowCredentials (usernameless flow), so it misses that rubric item despite otherwise strong coverage.

scenarios.name: fix-user-verification-error
scenarios.rationale: Both explain the default requireUserVerification: true versus 'preferred' mismatch and offer both fixes with consistency advice, but B more clearly states that verify doesn't read the options value and adds useful notes on authentication and storing userVerified, while A's UV-in-both-places framing is slightly less precise.
